newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industry seen competitive if dlr not too high.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industry seen competitive if dlr not too high.

text.p: Goods produced by American industry will remain competitive in world markets as long as the dollar does not become too strong, National Association of Manufacturers President Jerry Jasinowski said Wednesday.

Rejecting the notion that U.S. manufacturers had a "structural competitiveness" problem, Jasinowski called American industries' reduced share of exports in the 1980s a one-time event caused by a "misaligned exchange rate."

"As long as the exchange rate is not allowed to appreciate too far, American industry will remain competitive," he said in prepared testimony to the Senate Commerce subcommittee on manufacturing and competitiveness.
Jasinowski, one of several manufacturing officials to testify, called the current state of manufacturing quite good.

Since the 1980s, Jasinowski said manufacturers have overcome causes of stress that included not only "misaligned" exchange rates, but also an economic downturn, high interest rates and what he called excessive government regulation.

But he urged government to help today's restructured and healthier manufacturers by not raising interest rates, balancing the budget, offering tax, legal and regulatory relief and supporting U.S. trade abroad.
